topic.source_contract: Water-resource availability, abstraction and impoundment licensing, CAMS strategies, lawful rights and delivery evidence

facts.framework: National Framework for Water Resources 2025, updated 15 April 2026
facts.guard: regional strategy is not an abstraction right

facts.threshold: more than 20 cubic metres per day is likely to need a licence
facts.guard: threshold test is not confirmation that water is available

facts.application: licence types, pre-application and application route
facts.guard: application is not a granted licence

facts.availability: CAMS and abstraction licensing strategies describe local water availability
facts.guard: strategy status is not a parcel-specific licence or guaranteed yield
policy and trading potential are not completed rights transfer

scope_guards: Water-resource strategy is not treated as a granted abstraction licence.
The 20-cubic-metre threshold is not treated as proof that abstraction is environmentally acceptable.
A CAMS resource-availability status is not treated as guaranteed yield at an exact point.
A licence application is not treated as a granted, effective or transferable licence.
An abstraction licence is not treated as planning permission, land access or infrastructure consent.
Groundwater investigation consent is not treated as a production abstraction licence.
Trading potential is not treated as a completed licence transfer.
No score or promotion is written without exact source, availability, licence, land rights, infrastructure, monitoring and lawful operation evidence.
